cited_by.label: 1 Chronicles 15 · None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites
1 Chronicles 15 · None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites

precepts.text: The ark is hidden until Christ returns.
precepts.point: Do not let anyone claim the ark is in Ethiopia. The prophet Jeremiah hid the tabernacle, the ark, and the altar of incense in a cave, and it will not be found until the Most High gathers His people again.
precepts.why:
“And when Jeremy came thither, he found an hollow cave, wherein he laid the tabernacle, and the ark, and the altar of incense, and so stopped the door.” Some that followed him “came to mark the way, but they could not find it.” Jeremiah blamed them, saying, “As for that place, it shall be unknown until the time that God gather his people again together, and receive them unto mercy.”

In David's day the ark was with Israel, and David gathered all Israel to bring it up “from Kirjath–jearim”, the ark “of God the Lord, that dwelleth between the cherubims”. They carried it in a new cart and played before God with all their might, moving it to where David was so the priests could inquire.

But do not let anyone claim the ark is in Ethiopia. The prophet Jeremiah hid it in a cave with the tabernacle and the altar of incense, and it will not be found until the Most High gathers His people again. The ark is hidden until Christ returns.

precepts.text: The sons of Kohath were forbidden to touch the holy things lest they die; only the Levites bore the ark.
precepts.point: The anger of the Most High was kindled against Uzza, and He smote him because he put his hand to the ark, and he died there before the Most High. The ark was only to be touched by the Levites; the Most High does not play.
precepts.why:
When Aaron and his sons had covered the sanctuary and its vessels, “the sons of Kohath shall come to bear it: but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die.” The holy things were not to be handled; only the Levites bore the ark.

So when “the oxen stumbled”, and “Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark”, “the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzza, and he smote him, because he put his hand to the ark: and there he died before God.” The ark was only to be touched by the Levites. The Most High does not play.

precepts.text: The Philistines were smitten with emerods for holding the ark and begged Israel to take it away.
precepts.point: The ark blesses when it is with Israel and afflicts those who wrongly hold it, as when the Philistines were struck with emerods for taking it. If it falls, let it fall, and get a Levite to lift it.
precepts.why:
When the Philistines held the ark, “the hand of the Lord was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and smote them with emerods”. The men of Ashdod said, “The ark of the God of Israel shall not abide with us: for his hand is sore upon us, and upon Dagon our god.” They carried it about unto Gath, and there too “the hand of the Lord was against the city with a very great destruction”, and the men “had emerods in their secret parts.” The Philistines begged Israel to take it away.

The ark blesses when it is with Israel and afflicts those who wrongly hold it. After the breach upon Uzza, David was afraid and asked, “How shall I bring the ark of God home to me?” So he carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, where it remained three months, “And the Lord blessed the house of Obed–edom, and all that he had.”

The lesson of Uzza stands: if the ark falls, let it fall, and get a Levite to lift it.

precepts.text: Uzza handled the ark when he was not to and died for it, showing why this order matters.
precepts.point: He declared that none ought to carry the ark but the Levites, for the Most High had chosen them to carry it and to minister unto him forever.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 15: None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites

precepts.why:
“Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark; for the oxen stumbled. And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzza, and he smote him, because he put his hand to the ark: and there he died before God.” Uzza handled the ark when he was not to, and he died for it.

That shows why this order matters. David had seen what happens when the ark is not carried the way the Most High commanded, so now he says, “None ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites”.

moments.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: David consulted with the captains of thousands and hundreds and every leader, and proposed to all the congregation that they send abroad to their brethren everywhere, with the priests and Levites, to gather to them.
His purpose was to bring again the ark of the Most High, for they had not inquired at it in the days of Saul. All the congregation agreed, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.
David gathered all Israel from Shihor of Egypt to the entering of Hemath to bring the ark from Kirjath-jearim, and went up to Baalah, which is Kirjath-jearim, belonging to Judah.
They brought up the ark of the Most High, who dwelleth between the cherubims, carrying it in a new cart out of the house of Abinadab.

David and all Israel played before the Most High with all their might, with singing, harps, psalteries, timbrels, cymbals, and trumpets, as they moved the ark to where David was so the priests could inquire.
When they came to the threshingfloor of Chidon, the oxen stumbled and Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark.

The anger of the Most High was kindled against Uzza, and He smote him because he put his hand to the ark, and he died there before the Most High. The ark was only to be touched by the Levites; the Most High does not play.
David was displeased that the Most High had made a breach upon Uzza, and that place was called Perez-uzza. David was afraid that day and asked how he could bring the ark home.
David carried the ark aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, where it remained three months, and the Most High blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that he had.

“And David and all Israel played before God with all their might, and with singing”. David called for the ark of the covenant to come out. They're bringing it out, happy, singing, dancing, having a good time glorifying the Lord with the ark.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: “Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark; for the oxen stumbled.” The ark was shaking, and he put his hand out to stop it falling. “And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzza”. Only the priests, Aaron's sons, could deal with the ark. Only the high priest could touch it, Aaron and his sons. He did something he wasn't supposed to do. Good intentions, poor judgment.

“and he smote him, because he put his hand to the ark: and there he died before God.” He died because he touched it. Sometimes it's a knee-jerk reaction: something is falling, and you go to stop it. But he knew he wasn't supposed to touch it. The Lord told all Israel we can't touch the ark of the covenant; only the high priest could touch it. He had good intentions, but the result was terrible. He got put to death.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: “And David was afraid of God that day”. David got scared to death. Imagine somebody touching a damn ark and dropping dead right there on the spot. That's scary. The Lord ain't playing. I don't care if you have good intentions. If he says don't do it, don't do it. Some of our forefathers had great intentions and bad outcomes. For some people 'I meant well, I had good will, it was in my heart to help' is just a backup in case they do wrong.
